campaigns.tagline: Freedom is an order you give yourself.
campaigns.description: Lead Orin’s unbound dead out of servitude. Escape a quarry, defend a refuge, and break the Master’s bindings with unexpected living allies.
campaigns.shortDescription: The dead have broken their chains—but their Master wants them back.
campaigns.name: The Ashen Oath

missions.subtitle: The first order you give yourself.
missions.briefing: The Master’s binding broke at midnight. For the first time, Orin and the quarry’s dead can choose where to go. Orin leads them toward the northern gate before the guards can return them to servitude. Freedom begins with getting the company out alive.
hints: The guards watch the road more closely than the river.
Bare bones have little to fear from arrows.
Orin need not make the crossing alone.
The Ledgerkeeper guards his southern office. The road patrol and its mage pursue the company; the northern gate is the way out.

goals.label: Bring Orin to the northern quarry gate

intro.speaker: Orin
intro.text: The binding broke at midnight. I waited for another order. None came.

intro.speaker: A hollow voice
intro.text: Then give us one of our own.

intro.speaker: Orin
intro.text: We leave the quarry. Keep the archers behind the bones. If the mage finds me, there may not be a second midnight.

victory.speaker: Orin
victory.text: The gate is open. I thought freedom would sound louder.

victory.speaker: A hollow voice
victory.text: It sounds like no one telling us to go back.

victory.speaker: Orin
victory.text: There are empty houses west of here. Let us give them neighbors.

events.label: Recover the forgotten workers’ ledger

dialogue.speaker: Orin
dialogue.text: They wrote down our wages. They did not write down our names. Take the six coins. We can begin with that.

waves.label: An adept and warden arrive from the southern road on turn 6

missions.subtitle: A refuge needs neighbors, not another war.
missions.briefing: Orin’s company has found empty houses beside living villages. Captain Dain has orders to drive the dead away; the villagers want time to judge their new neighbors for themselves. Orin will defend the refuge while they gather. Helping the sick can win their support sooner, but a withdrawing soldier’s death would destroy the chance of peace.
hints: Defend ownership of the refuge through six enemy turns. Troops can leave the ruins to screen it; enemy recapture resets the count. Medicine reduces the defense to five turns.
Skeleton clubs punish the armored patrol. Bone bows answer its unarmored swordsmen, archers and adepts; protect those bows with a melee screen.
Nonlethal defensive attacks are allowed. Killing Dain or a retreating soldier ends mediation; check the combat preview before attacking and leave withdrawing men a way home.

goals.label: Defend the refuge until the villagers intervene

intro.speaker: Orin
intro.text: These houses are empty. The people next door are not. We could be neighbors, if they let us stay.

intro.speaker: Captain Dain
intro.text: My orders say the dead must leave. My patrol is coming to enforce them.

intro.speaker: Village elder
intro.text: Give us six days to gather the households. Defend your shelter if you must, but let men who turn back go home. There are sick families here who need the herbs in the northern grove.

intro.speaker: Orin
intro.text: Then we hold our ground. We will not hunt your wounded. And we will bring the medicine.

victory.speaker: Village elder
victory.text: Enough, Captain. They held their shelter and let your wounded leave. These houses are ours to offer. The dead may stay as our neighbors.

victory.speaker: Dain
victory.text: My orders did not mention people who would ask the dead to stay. Perhaps the man who wrote them left other things out.

victory.speaker: Orin
victory.text: He used to write my orders too. Come with us, and see what he has been hiding.

victory.speaker: Dain
victory.text: I will. My soldiers can rest here. I know which road we take next.

events.label: Bring medicine to the villagers

dialogue.speaker: Village elder
dialogue.text: The fever is easing. We will send word with the families you helped; the households will gather a day sooner. Take these six coins for your shelter.

dialogue.speaker: Orin
dialogue.text: We did not need the herbs ourselves. I am glad someone did.

warDialogue.speaker: Village elder
warDialogue.text: The herbs will still save lives. Take these six coins. But after the bloodshed, medicine alone cannot stop the patrol’s battle with you.

waves.label: An archer and swordsman arrive on turn 3

escalation.speaker: Village elder
escalation.text: There has been too much bloodshed for the patrol to accept our mediation. We cannot stop this battle for you.

escalation.speaker: Orin
escalation.text: Then there is no agreement left to make. We must break the patrol before we can leave.

warVictory.speaker: Orin
warVictory.text: The patrol is broken. But we have lost the chance to leave here with friends. We face the Master with our own company.

refuge.warBriefing: The attempt to live beside the villages has become an open battle. After the bloodshed, the households can no longer persuade the patrol to stand down. Orin’s company must break the remaining patrol to leave, and will face the Master without Dain’s help.
warHints: The patrol still has somewhere to run.
The empty houses remain, even after peace is lost.

missions.subtitle: Break the chains. Leave the names.
missions.briefing: Dain has chosen to stand beside Orin against the man who commanded them both. The Master still binds others to his will through stones along the road. Breaking those chains and confronting him is the company’s chance to secure a freedom he cannot simply revoke.
hints: Dain's hammer and the adepts answer bones; spears answer beasts. Withdraw wounded named allies before they are cut off.
The stones are where the Master’s reach begins.

goals.label: Break both binding stones
Defeat the Master

intro.speaker: The Master
intro.text: I gave you a second life. You owe me the use of it.

intro.speaker: Orin
intro.text: A life is not a ledger. These people choose whom they follow.

intro.speaker: Dain
intro.text: My wardens chose the same road. Break his binding stones. The adepts can answer his bones; my spears can keep the beasts off them.

victory.speaker: The Master
victory.text: Without me, what are you?

victory.speaker: Orin
victory.text: We have not decided yet. That is the point.

events.label: Recover the stolen names from the old archive

dialogue.speaker: Orin
dialogue.text: Here they are. All the names he took. We will return them, one house at a time.

waves.label: An unsealed binding stone raises a skeleton on turn 5
An unsealed binding stone raises a skeleton on turn 5
The Master's boar reaches the central road on turn 4

withoutDain.briefing: The refuge battle ended without an agreement. Dain and his allies will not come with Orin; the company must face the Master alone. His binding stones still hold others in servitude. Breaking them is the first step toward a freedom that can survive him.
hints: The dead will have to look after their own.
The stones are where the Master’s reach begins.

intro.speaker: The Master
intro.text: You broke the patrol that came to turn you back. You have learned my methods well.

intro.speaker: Orin
intro.text: We chose that battle. We will carry what it cost us. But you will not choose our lives again.

intro.speaker: A hollow voice
intro.text: No captain is coming to help us. Break the binding stones. We can still bring the others home.

ending.speaker: Dain
ending.text: What should I put in the new ledger?

ending.speaker: Orin
ending.text: Names first. And leave a blank page. We may become more than you expected.

campaigns.tagline: Neither shore can keep the tide alone.
campaigns.description: Lead Mira's merfolk through a drained estuary, rescue a salvage crew and coordinate two sluice gates. Open sea routes, sandbars, wooded shores and marsh channels reward different troops.
campaigns.shortDescription: The waters have receded, and a salvage crew hasn’t returned.
campaigns.name: The Borrowed Tide

missions.subtitle: Someone has borrowed tomorrow's tide.
missions.briefing: Rescue pilot Edda from the blocked estuary. Capture both sounding outworks and escort her to the fishing village, where she can show the townspeople why their boats are stranded.
missions.debrief: The outworks held a forged sluice order. Edda's soundings show water diverted into an abandoned quarry, exposing the wreck of a debt ship. The salvage factor is making workers recover its ledgers before anyone can compare the books.
hints: Merfolk can cross deep water and move normally on plains. Forests, groves and hills slow them and increase incoming damage.
Shallows are neutral for merfolk; swamps protect them. Land troops are exposed in both.
Keep Edda alive. Shore guards can reach Mira across the sandbars; protect the approaches while swimmers flank the outworks through deep water.

goals.label: Open both sounding outworks
Bring pilot Edda to the fishing village

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: The tide should have returned by dawn. Our nets are dry; their boats are on the mud. This is no quarrel either shore can afford.

intro.speaker: Edda
intro.text: Vale's men took the sounding posts. I saw a sluice order bearing the council seal, but the date was cut from an older sheet.

intro.speaker: Postmaster Harl
intro.text: Captain Vale sent us to hold these posts for the factor's salvage crew. Bring your accusation to the council; you will not cross here.

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: Then we take the posts and bring the pilot. Leave the fishing houses standing.

victory.speaker: Edda
victory.text: Here are my soundings, and his order. The quarry gate is open. The water did not disappear; someone moved it.

victory.speaker: Mira
victory.text: We cannot just close that gate. There are workers inside the wreck, below the next high tide.

events.label: Recover provisions from the southern fishing hamlet

dialogue.speaker: Fisher
dialogue.text: The factor bought our food on credit too. Take these nets and rations. Bring back the people he sent into that ship.

missions.subtitle: The books can wait. The workers cannot.
missions.briefing: Reach the wreck and recover the ledger. The rescue boat arrives at high tide on turn 6. Once the boat is here and the wreck is yours, defend it through three enemy turns to get the workers out.
missions.debrief: The last worker leaves with the ledger. Senn had paid Vale to seize the posts, then charged the villagers for salvage they never requested. Tomas deserted when ordered to burn the hull with workers inside. He knows the wooded route to the upper gate.
hints: Reach the wreck on the central sandbar. Rescue starts at high tide on turn 6; then defend it for three enemy turns.
Land allies use the northern sandbar and wooded shore; merfolk flank through sea and marshes.
Enemy recapture resets the rescue counter. You can leave the wreck, but keep it under your control.

goals.label: Recover the original ledger from the wreck
Defend the wreck through 3 enemy turns during the rescue

intro.speaker: Tomas
intro.text: I was hired to guard a salvage crew. Today Senn ordered us to set the ship alight. There are still people down there.

intro.speaker: Edda
intro.text: The rescue boat can enter this channel at high tide. First, get us to the wreck. Nobody touches the quarry gate while people are still inside.

intro.speaker: Foreman Cale
intro.text: The factor's ledger is company property. Clear the landing and burn the books.

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: A debt cannot give you ownership of a person. We take the wreck and get everyone out.

victory.speaker: Edda
victory.text: Last boat away. The clerk brought the books with her. Every order, every payment.

victory.speaker: Tomas
victory.text: Senn has shut the upper gate now. If we open only the lower one, the quarry water will flood the village. We need both controls and the beacon.

events.label: Recover the unaltered salvage ledger

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.text: These are the original accounts. He rewrote the council's order, then made each village pay for the delay. Keep them dry; I still have two colleagues below.

dialogue.speaker: Edda
dialogue.text: We have the wreck. Now wait for high tide on turn 6 so the rescue boat can reach us.

dialogue.speaker: Edda
dialogue.text: The boat is here. Hold the wreck for three turns while we bring the workers out.

dialogue.speaker: Edda
dialogue.text: High tide. The rescue boat is waiting. Get to the wreck so we can start.

waves.label: Senn's hired guard arrives along the wooded shore

Tomas.debrief: The workers leave with the ledger, but Tomas dies defending their escape. The rescued clerk explains that Senn's upper gate must open with the lower one to avoid flooding the village. His fellow deserters offer to guide the company along the wooded bank.

victory.speaker: Edda
victory.text: Last boat away. The clerk has the books. Tomas did not make it back.

victory.speaker: Mira
victory.text: We carry his testimony too. The clerk says we need both gates and the beacon; nobody else will die in a release we could have prevented.

missions.subtitle: One gate for the town, one for the sea.
missions.briefing: Capture the two sluice controls and escort Edda to the beacon. She will signal a safe release only after both gates are in your hands. Senn's guards defend the gates to prevent the council from discovering the diversion.
missions.debrief: At Edda's signal both controls release together. The estuary fills without a surge through the village. The recovered books reach the council; Senn loses his lease. The fishing towns and the reef appoint a shared tide crew, with neither shore allowed to operate a gate alone.
hints: Capture both forts: the upper sluice beside the wooded bank and the lower sluice beside the marsh. Bring Edda to the ruined beacon east of the lower channel; all three objectives are required.
Land allies can cross the northern sandbar to the wooded high bank. Swimmers can flank through deep water and the lower marsh channel. Guard the shallows back to Mira's keep.
Impact attacks break the armored gate guards; harpoons punish scouts and cover advancing allies. Wavemenders heal adjacent allies at turn start.

goals.label: Control both sluice gates
Bring Edda to the release beacon

intro.speaker: Tomas
intro.text: The high gate is reached through the woods. I can take that path. Your swimmers can reach the lower wheel through the reeds.

intro.speaker: Captain Vale
intro.text: You have taken a company's books and attacked its guards. Senn says the council will hang deserters first.

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: He forged the council's order. The clerk will testify. Stand aside and hear her, or answer for keeping this flood above the village.

intro.speaker: Edda
intro.text: They are staying. Bring me to the beacon. I will not signal until both wheels are ours.

victory.speaker: Edda
victory.text: Both flags up. Open together—now.

victory.speaker: Mira
victory.text: Watch the mudflats. There. The tide is home.

victory.speaker: Tomas
victory.text: And tomorrow?

victory.speaker: Mira
victory.text: Tomorrow we put someone from each shore beside each wheel.

events.label: Recover the southern ferry's supplies

dialogue.speaker: Boatkeeper
dialogue.text: We could not leave our homes, but we saved food for your company. Make sure that beacon means a safe tide.

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: Tomas's companions showed us the high bank through the woods. They will lead our land fighters. We take the lower wheel through the reeds.

intro.speaker: Captain Vale
intro.text: Senn says the council will hang deserters first. Your testimony will not save you.

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: He forged the council's order. Hear the clerk, or answer for holding this flood above the village.

intro.speaker: Edda
intro.text: Bring me to the beacon. I will signal only when both wheels are ours.

victory.speaker: Edda
victory.text: Both flags up. Open together—now.

victory.speaker: Mira
victory.text: The tide is home. Tomas should have seen it.

victory.speaker: Edda
victory.text: Put someone from each shore beside each wheel. Keep this from happening again.

ending.speaker: Edda
ending.text: The next sounding chart has two signatures. One from the quay, one from the reef.

ending.speaker: Mira
ending.text: And if the numbers disagree, we go out together and measure again.

campaigns.tagline: A forest and a village can share a road.
campaigns.description: Lead Alder’s woodland pack against an illegal logging operation. Capture its camps, uncover the missing workers’ fate, and bring the evidence to the village council across the river.
campaigns.shortDescription: The forest is falling, and the workers are disappearing.
campaigns.name: The Green Accord

missions.subtitle: Take their tools. Find the missing workers.
missions.briefing: The village council licenses ordinary timber cutting, but its Overseer has sent crews into Alder’s sacred groves. He claims the pack killed the missing woodcutters. His tools and carts are stored in two guarded logging camps. Capture both camps to stop the cutting, and recover the workers’ pay ledger from the northern ruin. Captain Dain commands the patrol protecting those camps; leave him alive if you can.
missions.debrief: Both logging camps are captured and the pay ledger contradicts the Overseer’s report. Dain suspends his patrol’s attacks and agrees to protect Lark’s investigation in the central grove. The Overseer’s other guards have accepted no truce.
hints: Capture both logging forts; standing in a marked grove does not stop the operation.
Search the northern ruin for the workers’ ledger.
Wolves cross woods easily. Boars and thorncaller staves fare better against armor.

goals.label: Capture both logging camps
Recover the workers’ pay ledger

intro.speaker: Lark
intro.text: The council promised the villages repair timber. Its Overseer marked our sacred groves instead. His crews keep their tools and carts in those two forts.

intro.speaker: Alder
intro.text: Take the camps and the cutting stops. The northern post kept the workers’ records. Bring those back too.

intro.speaker: Captain Dain
intro.text: My missing woodcutters were sent here. The Overseer says your pack killed them. I have orders to protect the crews that remain.

intro.speaker: Lark
intro.text: Your orders won’t tell us where they went. Their ledger might.

intro.speaker: Alder
intro.text: We need our roots back, not your bones. Keep away from our groves, captain, and help us find your people.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: Both camps are ours. Without their tools and carts, the crews have stopped cutting. Here is the ledger.

victory.speaker: Captain Dain
victory.text: These men were marked as deserters, but their wages went to the Overseer’s own account. That is his seal. I cannot explain it.

victory.speaker: Alder
victory.text: Lark can ask the grove what happened. Come and watch her work.

victory.speaker: Captain Dain
victory.text: Your pack has hurt my patrol, and mine has hurt yours. I am offering a truce for this investigation, not pretending that never happened.

events.label: Recover the workers’ pay ledger

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The missing crew refused to cut the sacred grove until their overdue wages were paid. Then they were ordered to report to the Rootbinder at the Overseer’s river works. Their pay was never collected.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Take the ledger. We can stop the cutting, but the roots must tell us what became of those workers.

withoutDain.briefing: Dain has fallen. Capture both logging camps to stop their crews, and recover the workers’ pay ledger from the northern ruin. His death does not answer what happened to the missing woodcutters; Lark must find evidence their families can hear without him.
withoutDain.debrief: The cutting operation has lost both camps. Dain died in the fighting; his death remains part of what happened. The ledger leads Lark to question the roots about the Rootbinder and the Overseer.
hints: Capture both logging forts; standing in a marked grove does not stop the operation.
Search the northern ruin for the workers’ ledger.
Wolves cross woods easily. Boars and thorncaller staves fare better against armor.

intro.speaker: Lark
intro.text: Dain is dead. His patrol’s orders still do not tell us what happened to the workers.

intro.speaker: Alder
intro.text: Take both tool camps and recover their ledger. We still owe the families an answer.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: The camps are ours and the cutting has stopped. The missing workers’ wages went to the Overseer, and their last orders sent them to the Rootbinder.

victory.speaker: Alder
victory.text: Dain will never hear their story. Lark, bring it back in a living branch. The families must be able to hear it for themselves.

missions.subtitle: A personal truce. An officer’s cover-up.
missions.briefing: Dain has suspended his patrol’s attacks and stands with Alder at the central grove. The Overseer, the council’s timber and toll officer, still commands the other paid charter guards. The ledger threatens his office; he calls Dain a mutineer and orders the grove silenced. Keep Lark in the central grove through three enemy turns while she listens to the workers’ memories. Dain is here to defend the investigation, not command the attacking guards.
missions.debrief: The vigil revealed a bargain: the Overseer supplied workers to the Rootbinder, who killed and bound them into unpaid logging crews. Lark carries their memories in a living branch. Dain will help bring that evidence to the village council; the Overseer’s false report can no longer be the only account.
hints: Move Lark into the central grove and protect her through three full enemy turns.
Leaving the grove or losing ownership resets the vigil.
Dain is your ally; the Overseer’s remaining charter guards are the enemy.

goals.label: Protect Lark in the central grove through three enemy turns

intro.speaker: Captain Dain
intro.text: I suspended my patrol’s orders. These other guards answer to the Overseer. I will stand here with you until we know what happened.

intro.speaker: The Overseer
intro.text: Dain is dismissed. His truce binds none of you. Destroy the branch and break their circle before the council hears their lies.

intro.speaker: Lark
intro.text: Bring me to the central grove. The roots kept the workers’ last memories. If I am driven out, I must begin again.

intro.speaker: Alder
intro.text: Then we defend the grove, captain included. The Overseer has given us a reason to keep listening.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: The workers asked for the pay he owed them and refused to cut this grove. The Overseer handed them to the Rootbinder. He killed them and bound their bodies to the logging crews.

victory.speaker: Captain Dain
victory.text: Unpaid labor for the Overseer. Bodies and protection for the Rootbinder. And my patrol sent to punish you for their murders.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: This branch holds what the roots remember. Their families can hear it too.

victory.speaker: Alder
victory.text: The council is meeting across the river. We take the branch and the ledger there. Let the people who gave him his office judge what he did with it.

events.label: Recover the northern guard-post supplies

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: The abandoned guard post still has funds for provisions. Use them to bring another defender to the grove; Lark cannot finish her work if we lose it.

waves.label: A warden and archer arrive from the east on turn 3
An adept and soldier arrive from the east on turn 5

withoutDain.briefing: Dain is dead. The ledger still names the Overseer and the Rootbinder, but the council needs more than accusations from the pack. Keep Lark in the central grove through three full enemy turns so she can carry the workers’ memories in a living branch. The Overseer’s remaining charter guards are attacking to destroy that evidence.
withoutDain.debrief: The roots revealed the workers’ murder and binding. Dain cannot testify, but the living branch carries their memories. The pack must take it and the ledger to the council across the river.
hints: Protect Lark in the grove through three enemy turns.
Leaving or losing the grove resets the vigil.

intro.speaker: Lark
intro.text: Dain cannot be our witness. The roots can. Keep me in the central grove while I listen.

intro.speaker: The Overseer
intro.text: The captain is dead. Destroy that branch before the council hears a word of this.

intro.speaker: Alder
intro.text: They will hear the workers themselves. We defend the grove until Lark has their memories.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: The workers demanded their wages and refused to cut the grove. The Overseer delivered them to the Rootbinder; he killed and bound them into his logging crews.

victory.speaker: Alder
victory.text: Dain is among the dead now too. We cannot undo that. Bring the branch and the ledger to the families, and let them judge the whole account.

missions.subtitle: A witness, a bridge, and a promise.
missions.briefing: The village council is meeting at the northern village across the river. Lark’s branch carries the murdered workers’ memories; the ledger and Dain’s testimony identify the Overseer who supplied them to the Rootbinder. The necromancer has barred the crossing to protect that bargain. Capture the bridge fort so the households can cross safely, and bring Lark to the meeting alive. Tamsin, a village adept, joins the escort against the bound dead.
missions.debrief: Lark delivered the memories and the bridge fort remains secure. The council revoked the Overseer’s timber and toll charter. The villages and Alder’s pack agreed to protect the crossing and spare the sacred groves. The Rootbinder may still threaten the valley; this victory delivered the truth and established a road both peoples can defend.
hints: The northern trees may offer a gentler journey.
A witness need not stand in the front rank.

goals.label: Secure the fort beside the bridge
Bring Lark to the northern village

intro.speaker: Captain Dain
intro.text: The council gave the Overseer his timber and toll charter. With the ledger and the workers’ memories, they can take it away. I will answer for my patrol’s part as well.

intro.speaker: Lark
intro.text: The Rootbinder has put his dead on the crossing. He needs the Overseer’s protection and his supply of bodies. He would rather burn this branch than let the families hear it.

intro.speaker: Alder
intro.text: Take the bridge fort so the households can cross. Bring Lark to the northern meeting alive; a dead necromancer alone will not open a shared road.

intro.speaker: Tamsin
intro.text: Dain sent for me. Some of those workers were my neighbors. Stone sparks crack bone; let the shields hold the dead while I clear your road.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: The families heard the branch. The council matched the orders to the ledger and revoked the Overseer’s charter.

victory.speaker: Captain Dain
victory.text: I have given them my account too. We will harvest the ordinary woods for repairs. Your groves are outside the charter.

victory.speaker: Alder
victory.text: The fort is ours. Village and woodland guards can keep this road together; neither side owns the right to close it.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: The Rootbinder still has his dead. But he no longer has a silent village to hide them in.

events.label: Recover provisions from the old crossing post

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The old crossing post has provisions for a stranded escort. Bring another shield to the road; the families are waiting on the other bank.

withoutDain.briefing: Dain is dead, but Lark’s living branch carries the workers’ memories and the ledger records their last orders. Tamsin, an adept from the villages, has joined the escort to help bring that evidence to the council. The Rootbinder bars the river to protect his supply of bodies. Capture the bridge fort and bring Lark to the northern meeting alive.
withoutDain.debrief: The council heard the branch, examined the ledger and learned of Dain’s death. It revoked the Overseer’s charter and agreed to protect the road with the pack. The Rootbinder remains a danger, but the workers’ murder is exposed and the crossing is held.
hints: The northern trees may offer a gentler journey.
A witness need not stand in the front rank.

intro.speaker: Tamsin
intro.text: I came from the villages to help you reach the council. The workers were our neighbors. Dain cannot speak; their families must hear this branch.

intro.speaker: Lark
intro.text: The Rootbinder wants his bargain kept hidden. The branch and the ledger must reach the northern village.

intro.speaker: Alder
intro.text: Take the bridge fort and protect Lark. We owe the families an open road and an honest account, including Dain’s death.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: The families heard the workers’ memories. We told them about Dain too. The council has revoked the Overseer’s charter.

victory.speaker: Alder
victory.text: The fort is ours. The households will help us guard the crossing and keep the sacred groves outside their timber cutting.

victory.speaker: Lark
victory.text: Then let the first travelers cross. We have enough graves; we need neighbors.

ending.speaker: Lark
ending.text: The first cart crossed today. It carried apples, not axes.

ending.speaker: Alder
ending.text: Keep the road open. The roots will do the rest.

campaigns.tagline: A dark crossing. A road into the missing villages.
campaigns.description: Lead Captain Nera’s patrol across a river whose far bank has gone dark. Find the ferryman, reopen the village road, and follow the people taken by the dead.
campaigns.shortDescription: Investigate the dark eastern bank and follow the missing villagers.
campaigns.name: The Lantern Road

missions.subtitle: Find out why the other bank went dark.
missions.briefing: The landing lamp has gone out. Across the river, every window is dark. The ferry is tied up on the far bank, and nobody answers from the crossing. Take the island fords and find the ferryman.
missions.debrief: The patrol reached the ferryman and secured the eastern villages.
hints: Find the scouts in the western woods to reinforce your patrol.

goals.label: Reach the ferryman’s house
Light and secure the eastern villages

intro.speaker: Ivo
intro.text: That landing lamp has burned every night since I was a boy. Last night it went out. So did every window on the other bank.

intro.speaker: Nera
intro.text: And the ferry?

intro.speaker: Ivo
intro.text: Still tied up over there. We’ll have to take the fords round the island.

intro.speaker: Oren
intro.text: The wind’s coming down the valley. That mist is creeping the other way.

intro.speaker: Ivo
intro.text: You studied fog?

intro.speaker: Oren
intro.text: A whole winter at the Collegium. This wasn’t in the lessons.

intro.speaker: Nera
intro.text: Find the ferryman. Quickly. Whatever happened, he’s alone over there.

victory.speaker: Nera
victory.text: Both lanterns are burning. Leave someone watching the crossing; the rest of us take the eastern road. We still have people to find.

events.label: A scouting patrol joins the company

dialogue.speaker: Scout
dialogue.text: You’re the patrol? We’ve been checking the western woods. Nobody has come back across the ford. I’ll show you the way.

events.label: A scouting patrol joins the company

dialogue.speaker: Scout
dialogue.text: No sign of raiders on this bank. Whatever stopped the ferry is across the river. I’m coming with you.

events.label: A scouting patrol joins the company

dialogue.speaker: Scout
dialogue.text: The mountain path is quiet. The old quarry cave isn’t. We heard something breathing in there. Leave it alone if you’re in a hurry.

events.label: A bear emerges from the cave
Three bats burst from the island woods

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: Bats! Keep them off the horses!

dialogue.speaker: Oren
dialogue.text: There are accounts of swarms like this in the old siege chronicles. I thought the writers were embellishing.

events.label: The skeletons notice the patrol
The patrol enters the ferryman’s house and lights its lantern
A cry from the ferryman’s house

dialogue.speaker: Ferryman
dialogue.text: Over here! They’re at the door! For the love of anything living, get them away from the door!

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: Shields up. Make them come to us.

events.label: No voice answers from the house

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: No lamp. No answer. Get to the house.

events.label: The ferryman is alive

dialogue.speaker: Ferryman
dialogue.text: I thought the door would give before anyone heard me.

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: We saw the landing lantern go out. Where is everyone?

dialogue.speaker: Ferryman
dialogue.text: The dead took them. Went house to house, drove them out onto the eastern road. I barred this door and put the lamp out.

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: Stay inside. We’ll light the villages and see what’s left.

events.label: A letter lies beside the extinguished lamp

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: The door is broken. We’re too late.

dialogue.speaker: The letter
dialogue.text: If someone finds this: skeletons took the villagers up the eastern road. I stayed to keep the ferry ready. They have come back for me. Leave the light out. Save yourselves.

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: We’re lighting it. Then we follow the road.

events.label: The mage questions the ferryman

dialogue.speaker: Oren
dialogue.text: Who gave the skeletons their orders? Did you see him?

dialogue.speaker: Ferryman
dialogue.text: Something in a robe. Bare bone where its face should be. The other dead stood still when it spoke.

dialogue.speaker: Oren
dialogue.text: A lich. Those villages weren’t attacked for their coin.

dialogue.speaker: Ferryman
dialogue.text: Then bring my neighbors back. And watch the houses. I heard things moving inside after the people were gone.

events.label: Spiders emerge from the village
Spiders emerge from the village
Giant spiders spill out of the houses

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: Spiders! Back from the doorway!

dialogue.speaker: Oren
dialogue.text: Cellar spiders. We raised them at the Collegium. All the food in the world wouldn’t make them grow like this.

events.label: The eastern villages are lit and the spiders are defeated

item.name: Quarry hammer
item.description: Recovered from the old quarry. Its heavy head delivers a single crushing blow.

events.label: Nera takes a quarry hammer

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: Quarry tools. This hammer still has a sound head. I’ll take it.

missions.subtitle: Three crossings. Three homes to reclaim.
missions.briefing: Beyond the crossing, three roadside settlements are held by the dead. Nera’s patrol joins Warden Sella’s relief party to reopen the route. The Tollkeeper commands this stretch of road; the company needs the villages and their shelter, not just his head.
hints: One bridge need not carry the whole army.
A welcoming village can keep a march alive. Stone sparks punish bones; shield their fragile adepts with infantry.
The southern bone bow arrives on turn 7. Capture and defend all three villages together, rotating wounded troops into friendly shelter.

goals.label: Light all three eastern villages

intro.speaker: Warden Sella
intro.text: Their bowmen are watching the bridge. My spears can hold the banks, but the skeletons will barely feel their points.

intro.speaker: Nera
intro.text: Hold the approaches. Scouts, find another crossing. We need those villages open to the living.

victory.speaker: Warden Sella
victory.text: All three windows are lit. One family even lent us their kettle.

victory.speaker: Ivo
victory.text: There is still a bell sounding in the marsh. Every time it rings, another grave opens.

victory.speaker: Nera
victory.text: Then we go to the bell.

events.label: Recover the southern road cache

dialogue.speaker: Ivo
dialogue.text: Dry blankets, clean bandages, and six coins. Someone expected the road to open again. I would hate to disappoint them.

events.label: The ferryman’s emergency purse supplies the next patrol

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: The ferryman pressed his emergency purse into my hand. Six coins. We’ll use them to bring his neighbors home.

events.label: The ferryman’s letter points the way

dialogue.speaker: Nera
dialogue.text: He left us a road to follow. We owe him more than a lamp in the window.

waves.label: Two skeletons enter from the eastern road on turn 5
A bone bow reaches the southern crossing on turn 7

missions.subtitle: Silence the graves before silencing the bell.
missions.briefing: The villages are lit again, but the bell keeps calling their dead back to war. Nera and the adepts have traced that call to the grave ruins. Breaking those bindings will let the company silence the Bellwarden and leave the valley a road home.
hints: The broken walls still cast a useful shadow.
Listen for where the bell’s answer comes from.

goals.label: Use an adept to seal the three grave ruins
Defeat the Bellwarden

intro.speaker: Adept Meri
intro.text: The bell does not make the dead. It calls them from these graves. Stand on a grave and I can close the binding.

intro.speaker: Nera
intro.text: We can hit the walls all day and still lose the road. Seal the flanks, protect Meri, then take the bell.

intro.speaker: Meri
intro.text: My stone sparks hurt bones. Do keep their swords away from me.

victory.speaker: Ivo
victory.text: It stopped. Listen. Just frogs.

victory.speaker: Nera
victory.text: That is a better bell than any I have heard.

events.label: Meet the reed gatherers by the northern bridge

dialogue.speaker: Reed gatherer
dialogue.text: We saved what we could. Please make sure the road is still open when our children come home.

waves.label: An unsealed grave raises a skeleton on turn 8
An unsealed grave raises a skeleton on turn 8
An unsealed grave raises a skeleton on turn 8
An unsealed grave raises a skeleton on turn 12
An unsealed grave raises a skeleton on turn 12
An unsealed grave raises a skeleton on turn 12

ending.speaker: Nera
ending.text: Leave a watch at every crossing. Carry lamps down the road. We opened the valley; now we keep it open.
